Courses 
* Course List: https://irt.seoultech.ac.kr/
The finalized list of courses offered in English for each semester will be available one month 
before the start of the semester. In the meantime, please refer to the course list from the previous 
year. Please note that exchange students are allowed to select courses only from the Module list.
* Syllabus
For students’ convenience, we have gathered all the syllabi for the Module courses on Google Drive.
- (2026 Spring Semester) https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1pUOZuQxGcJMlihgKEX0tN1phAWr7EVID?usp=sharing
- (2025 Fall Semester) https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1pUOZuQxGcJMlihgKEX0tN1phAWr7EVID?usp=sharing
The course list for each semester at SeoulTech is announced approximately six weeks before the start of 
the semester. Students may refer to the previous year’s course list when considering whether to apply to 
SeoulTech. However, please note that some courses may be added or removed for the upcoming semester.
As course offerings are relatively flexible, students whose home universities have strict academic 
requirements—such as specific courses that must be taken—should be aware that SeoulTech cannot 
guarantee the availability of particular courses. Since course offerings may change, students are advised to 
take this into consideration when applying.
Intensive Korean Language Course Program (https://klc.seoultech.ac.kr/en/course/registration/)
Exchange students may enroll in an intensive Korean language course. This is a non-credit 
course, and students are required to pay the tuition fee.

Grading System
All exchange students can take 2 credits ~ 18 credits per semester. 
1 Credit = 16 teaching hours including lectures, exam, assignments, and attendance
1 Course = 2 or 3 credits
Each course lasts a semester(16 weeks). 
Assessment
 ※ The lowest passing grade is D0(60.)
Living in SEOULTECH
■ On campus
SeoulTech guarantees accommodation in the Sunglim Dormitory for exchange students.
Please note that there are very limited spaces available in the International Hall. In addition, 
current residents are given priority to remain in the same room for the following semester. 
Therefore, the chances of being assigned to the International Hall are very low.
For this reason, we only accept applications for the International Hall on a waiting list basis. 
While accommodation in the Sunglim Dormitory is guaranteed, placement in the International 
Hall is NOT guaranteed.

Language requirement
SeoulTech requires a good command of English (B2 level) or Korean (TOPIK Level 3) in order 
to communicate and function effectively in an academic environment.
An internationally recognized language certificate equivalent to the B2 level is required:
; TOEIC 750/ IELTS 5.5/ TOEFL 72 /Cambridge English Scale 160 / Global Scale of English (Pearson) 59 
or
: Topik(Test of Proficiency in Korean) 3
* Please note that students who apply to the exchange program using a TOPIK score will be 
permitted to enroll in Korean-language-taught courses only.
Insurance
National Health Insurance is a mandatory program implemented by the Ministry of Health and 
Welfare in Korea and is not optional. It applies regardless of whether students have private 
insurance. Once foreign registration is completed after arrival in Korea, students’ information will 
be updated in the National Health Insurance system, and students will be automatically enrolled. 
★ Additional documents (applicable only to students from non-OECD countries)
 1. A bank statement showing the account balance
 2. A certificate of enrollment from the current home university, 
    notarized by the Korean Embassy or apostilled
 ** Please note that the classification of non-OECD countries is determined based on 
the student’s nationality(passport), not the country where the student is currently studying.
 ** These two documents must be sent by post to the SeoulTech Office of International
Affairs no later than two weeks before student’s arrival in Korea.

FACTSHEET_SEOULTECH 6
As of 2026, the monthly National Health Insurance premium is KRW 79,310. A payment notice 
is sent each month to the student’s registered residence in Korea.
Visa
A student visa (D-2-6) is required for individuals who are not of Korean nationality in order to study 
in Korea. Please note that a visitor visa cannot be changed to a student visa within Korea. Students 
must apply for a D-2-6 student visa prior to arrival.
The Ministry of Justice introduced new regulations in June 2022 and strengthened immigration policies. 
As a result, additional documents are required for exchange students from non-OECD countries.
* Students from OECD countries 
  Normally, the following three documents are sufficient to apply for a student visa (D-2-6):
  - Certificate of Admission
  - Letter of Acceptance
  - Certificate of Business Registration
* Students from Non-OECD countries 
  The Ministry of Justice has strengthened immigration policies and requires additional 
documents, even for exchange students. 
  - Bank statement: The statement must demonstrate sufficient funds to cover living expenses 
during the exchange period (USD 6,000 for one semester / USD 12,000 for one academic year).
  - Certificate of Enrollment: This document must be apostilled or notarized by the Korean 
Embassy in the student’s country of study.
※ These two documents must be sent by post to the SeoulTech Office of International Affairs 
no later than two weeks before student’s arrival in Korea. If the documents are not received 
by then, your previously issued student visa may be cancelled upon SeoulTech’s request.
※ Important Note on Nationality: > The classification of "OECD" or "Non-OECD" countries is 
based strictly on the student's nationality (as indicated on their passport), not the location of 
their home university. (Example) A Cambodia student studying at a university in the 
Germany is classified as a "Non-OECD" student.
Korean buddy program & International Student Club(ISC)
ISC (International Student Club) is a student organization at SeoulTech that serves as a buddy program 
for international students. During their stay in Korea, exchange students are supported by ISC members 
to help make their campus life more enjoyable and enriching.
